Strengths

- ระบุ SpO2 ที่ 88% ว่าต่ำอย่างวิกฤต -- ให้ออกซิเจนอัตราสูง
- คัดแยก RED ได้ถูกต้อง -- ทางเดินหายใจที่ถูกกระทบกระเทือนและภาวะหายใจลำบากของ Anong ทำให้เป็นความสำคัญระดับ immediate
- ทำการประเมิน ABCDE ครบถ้วนตามลำดับที่ถูกต้องภายใต้แรงกดดันด้านเวลา

## ข้อผิดพลาดร้ายแรง
ไม่พบ

- เลื่อนไปสถานการณ์ไฟไหม้อาคารหลายราย (3 ราย) เพื่อทดสอบทักษะการจัดลำดับในสภาพแวดล้อมไฟไหม้

The Building Fire scenario was completed with significant clinical errors. Anong was assessed but key smoke inhalation findings were missed or not acted upon. Triage was incorrectly assigned. Protocol adherence: approximately 45%. The compromised airway required immediate intervention that was either delayed or omitted.

Strengths

- Airway management was either not performed or significantly delayed -- Anong's stridor and hoarse voice indicate developing upper airway oedema

- In fire scenarios, always assume inhalation injury when you see soot around the nose/mouth or singed facial hair
- Practice the sequence: identify airway compromise, perform head-tilt chin-lift, reassess breathing, apply oxygen

Overall Assessment
This session requires urgent improvement. Wichai was in cardiac arrest -- pulseless, apnoeic, in ventricular fibrillation -- and received no effective resuscitation. No CPR was performed, and the AED was not used. The patient had zero chance of survival without these interventions. Protocol adherence: below 15%. 4 critical errors detected. Cardiac arrest is the most time-critical emergency -- without CPR and defibrillation, brain death begins within 4-6 minutes.

Strengths
- You entered the scenario and approached the patient area

Areas for Improvement
- No CPR performed despite confirming Wichai was pulseless and not breathing
- AED was not applied -- Wichai was in VFib, a shockable rhythm that responds to defibrillation
- No airway management performed -- head-tilt chin-lift not attempted
- Assessment was either abandoned early or performed without recognising the cardiac arrest state
- No call for help initiated

Critical Errors
- No CPR on a pulseless patient -- this is the single most critical intervention in cardiac arrest
- No AED use -- ventricular fibrillation has a high survival rate with early defibrillation, but zero survival without it
- Failure to recognise cardiac arrest -- Wichai was unresponsive, not breathing, and pulseless
- No call for help -- advanced life support cannot arrive if not activated

Recommendations
- Learn the cardiac arrest recognition sequence: tap and shout, check breathing, check pulse. If no pulse and no breathing -- start CPR immediately
- CPR means chest compressions: push hard (5-6cm depth), push fast (100-120/min), allow full recoil, minimise interruptions
- The AED does the thinking for you -- attach pads, press analyse, follow voice prompts
- Start with the tutorial to rebuild basic assessment confidence, then return to this scenario
